conflicts.description: The same broad audiovisual-work concept is named title in IMDb and film in Sakila, with different identifier names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both under the work entity with snake_case work terminology and source-scoped work identifiers.

conflicts.description: IMDb represents a credited person name as primaryname, while Sakila calls the entity actor and separates first and last names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the entity as person while retaining display_name separately from atomic given_name and family_name.

conflicts.description: IMDb uses genre terminology while Sakila uses category for a comparable film classification concept.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the concept as genre and preserved source category identifiers as genre identifiers.

conflicts.description: The source term inventory identifies an individual physical copy rather than an aggregate stock measure.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the target entity and key to inventory_item and inventory_item_id.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are declared as number even though their descriptions define string identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Typed all IMDb identifiers as string in the target.

conflicts.description: IMDb primarytitle is declared integer but described as title text.
conflicts.resolution: Typed primary_title as string.

conflicts.description: Calendar years are represented as strings in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Typed year attributes as integer, treating source null markers as null values.

conflicts.description: Numeric durations and monetary values are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed durations as integer quantities and monetary values as number.

conflicts.description: Logical active flags are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed active-state fields as boolean.

conflicts.description: Fields described as containing date and time are declared as date.
conflicts.resolution: Typed event and update timestamps as datetime.

conflicts.description: Runtime is represented in minutes in both sources, which is not the selected standard SI duration unit.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized runtime as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is represented in days.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the rental period as seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb average rating is a numeric user score, whereas Sakila rating is a categorical audience classification.
conflicts.resolution: Kept these as separate average_rating and content_rating attributes rather than conflating their scales.

conflicts.description: Primary/display titles and original-language titles have distinct semantics despite all being title text.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped display titles to primary_title and retained original_title as a separate attribute.

conflicts.description: Current release language, original work language, and alternate-title language play different semantic roles.
conflicts.resolution: Retained distinct foreign-key roles on work and alternate_title while sharing a normalized language entity.

conflicts.description: Monetary values lack an explicit source currency.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved numeric amounts without inventing a currency code and documented reliance on the source system currency.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns encode arrays or multi-value attributes inside strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized each multi-value attribute into child or bridge resources with atomic values and explicit foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates searchable film text in film_text while core film attributes reside in film.
conflicts.resolution: Merged duplicate title and description attributes into work with provenance from both tables.

conflicts.description: IMDb models title metadata only, while Sakila separates catalog works, physical copies, and rental transactions.
conflicts.resolution: Retained normalized work, inventory_item, and rental entities so catalog identity is not conflated with physical-copy or transaction identity.

conflicts.description: The address location is an opaque geometry value whose internal geometry kind and components are unspecified.
conflicts.resolution: Retained it as a single serialized geometry field rather than inventing latitude/longitude semantics not supplied by the source.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to several genres per title, whereas Sakila expresses film categories through a many-to-many bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized both as the many-to-many work_genre relationship.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds multiple directors and writers in one crew row, while Sakila uses rows in a film-actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Exploded IMDb arrays into work_director and work_writer bridges and represented principal/cast associations in work_credit.

conflicts.description: A person can be known for several works and a work can be associated with several persons.
conflicts.resolution: Created the many-to-many person_known_work bridge.

conflicts.description: Episodes and series are both titles linked by a recursive one-to-many relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Created episode as a relationship resource with separate episode and parent-series foreign keys to work.

conflicts.description: One catalog film can have many physical inventory copies.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved work-to-inventory_item as a one-to-many relationship.

conflicts.description: Equivalent work entities use incompatible natural-looking alphanumeric and surrogate identifiers, and film_text omits an explicit key declaration.
conflicts.resolution: Defined source-scoped string work_id as the unified key and included all corresponding source identifiers in its provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent credited-person entities use different identifier systems.
conflicts.resolution: Defined a source-scoped string person_id with both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: IMDb alternate titles have no declared primary key although ordering is unique only within a title.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic alternate_title_id and retained ordering as a non-identity sequence attribute.

conflicts.description: Credit rows have no common declared key; IMDb uses per-title ordering while Sakila identifies associations through foreign-key pairs.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic credit_id so source-specific sequence and relationship keys remain semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Sakila provides a payment identifier described as a surrogate key but does not declare a table primary key.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted payment_id to the target payment primary key.

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare no primary keys despite representing unique entity associations.
conflicts.resolution: Used the corresponding foreign-key pairs as composite target keys where the association has no additional row identity.

conflicts.description: The same broad person/performer concept is named name in IMDb and actor in Sakila, with different identifier and name-column conventions.
conflicts.resolution: A unified person resource was created. Source identifiers feed person_id, while IMDb display_name remains distinct from Sakila's atomic first_name and last_name because they are not semantically interchangeable.

conflicts.description: Audiovisual works are called titles in IMDb and films in Sakila; title columns also use primarytitle versus title.
conflicts.resolution: The entities were unified as work, and equivalent display-title values were named primary_title.

conflicts.description: IMDb calls work classifications genres while Sakila calls them categories.
conflicts.resolution: Both are represented by neutral classification and work_classification resources.

conflicts.description: Equivalent duration attributes use different names.
conflicts.resolution: They were unified as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are incorrectly declared as number in several source resources despite descriptions specifying strings.
conflicts.resolution: All alphanumeric IMDb identifiers are represented as string.

conflicts.description: IMDb primarytitle is declared integer although its description defines textual content.
conflicts.resolution: primary_title is typed string.

conflicts.description: Calendar years are represented as strings in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Valid years are typed integer, with source null sentinels treated as missing values.

conflicts.description: Durations and monetary amounts are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Durations are numeric integer seconds and monetary values are number, without inventing an unavailable currency.

conflicts.description: Boolean status flags are encoded as strings.
conflicts.resolution: The target uses boolean is_active fields.

conflicts.description: Source fields described as date-and-time values are typed date.
conflicts.resolution: The target uses datetime for event timestamps.

conflicts.description: Foreign-key columns use integer while their referenced source primary keys are declared string.
conflicts.resolution: Target foreign and primary key types are consistently string.

conflicts.description: Runtime is stored in minutes rather than the target's standard physical unit.
conflicts.resolution: Runtime is standardized to SI seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is expressed in days.
conflicts.resolution: Rental duration is standardized to SI seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb average user rating is a numeric preference score, while Sakila rating is a categorical audience content classification.
conflicts.resolution: The semantically distinct values remain separate as average_user_rating and content_rating.

conflicts.description: IMDb alias language is a free code or label, whereas Sakila uses a keyed language entity for a film's language.
conflicts.resolution: Alias language remains language_code on work_alias; Sakila film language relationships use language_id and are not conflated.

conflicts.description: IMDb supplies a credited display name, while Sakila separates legal-style given and family names.
conflicts.resolution: display_name, first_name, and last_name remain distinct to avoid asserting equivalence between different name semantics.

conflicts.description: IMDb startyear can mean series start year, while Sakila release_year is a film release year.
conflicts.resolution: The unified attribute is explicitly named release_start_year to preserve the shared inception-year meaning without implying every work is a film.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns contain arrays or multi-value content inside scalar strings.
conflicts.resolution: Values were atomized into person_profession, person_known_work, work_classification, work_alias_type, work_alias_attribute, work_credit, and work_special_feature rows.

conflicts.description: Credits are decomposed differently: IMDb has principal-credit rows plus director/writer arrays, while Sakila has a film-actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: All are normalized into work_credit with foreign keys to work and person and optional role-specific attributes.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates title and description in a separate full-text support table.
conflicts.resolution: Semantically identical film_text attributes are merged into work rather than preserving a duplicate entity.

conflicts.description: A point geometry is carried as one non-generic composite string.
conflicts.resolution: It is split into atomic numeric latitude and longitude fields compatible with generic Frictionless types.

conflicts.description: Episode hierarchy is stored as a relationship table separate from title basics.
conflicts.resolution: A normalized episode subtype/relationship resource references work twice, once for the episode and once for its parent.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to three genres in each title row, while Sakila models a many-to-many film-category relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Both are represented as the N:M work_classification bridge.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds a one-to-many list of known works in each person row.
conflicts.resolution: The list is represented as person_known_work, allowing multiple works per person and multiple people per work.

conflicts.description: Contributor relationships vary between arrays, ordered principal rows, and an explicit many-to-many actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: A row-per-person-per-credit representation is used in work_credit; repeated characters can produce separate atomic credit rows.

conflicts.description: Each alias can have multiple types and multiple descriptive attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Separate one-to-many child resources preserve each atomic type and attribute.

conflicts.description: Ratings are conceptually optional one-to-one data for a work but are stored in a separate resource without an explicit primary key.
conflicts.resolution: work_rating uses work_id as its primary key and foreign key, enforcing at most one aggregate rating row per work.

conflicts.description: Unified people have incompatible source key domains: IMDb natural-style alphanumeric identifiers and Sakila surrogate actor identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Both source primary keys map to string person_id, with source-system identity retained during integration to prevent collisions.

conflicts.description: Unified works use different source identifiers and key styles.
conflicts.resolution: Both primary keys map to string work_id, with source-system identity retained during integration.

conflicts.description: title_akas has no declared primary key although ordering is documented as unique within a title.
conflicts.resolution: work_alias uses the composite key work_id plus alias_order.

conflicts.description: title_episode has no declared primary key even though each episode work has one parent-series relationship.
conflicts.resolution: episode_work_id is the primary key and also a foreign key to work.

conflicts.description: title_ratings lacks a declared primary key despite containing one aggregate row per title.
conflicts.resolution: work_id is used as the work_rating primary key.

conflicts.description: payment has no declared primary key although payment_id is described as its unique surrogate identifier.
conflicts.resolution: payment_id is promoted to the required target primary key.

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare foreign keys but no primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized bridges use relationship-based keys where the relationship is unique; work_credit instead uses a synthetic credit_id because richer IMDb credits can repeat a work-person pair.

conflicts.description: Store and staff form a cyclic foreign-key dependency.
conflicts.resolution: Both relationships are retained because they represent different semantics: a store's manager and a staff member's home store.

conflicts.description: The same broad media-work concept is named title in IMDb and film in Sakila, with different identifier names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the concepts under media_title with a canonical source-qualified media_title_id.

conflicts.description: IMDb calls the entity a name/person while Sakila models the overlapping acting subset as actor.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both under person while retaining source-specific name representations.

conflicts.description: IMDb uses genre terminology while Sakila uses category for media classification.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the classification entity as category and its label as category_name.

conflicts.description: Equivalent duration attributes use different names.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the attribute as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: The source table name inventory can denote either a collection or an individual copy.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the row-level entity to inventory_item and its key to inventory_item_id.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are incorrectly declared as number despite descriptions specifying strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed all canonical IMDb-derived identifiers as string.

conflicts.description: The primary title is declared integer but described as text.
conflicts.resolution: Typed primary_title as string.

conflicts.description: Year values are represented as strings and may contain source null markers.
conflicts.resolution: Typed valid normalized years as integer and treated source null markers as missing values.

conflicts.description: Numeric durations and monetary amounts are represented as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed durations and amounts as number after normalization.

conflicts.description: Boolean status values are represented as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed normalized activity indicators as boolean.

conflicts.description: Fields declared as date are described or conventionally used as timestamps.
conflicts.resolution: Used datetime where time-of-day semantics are present or updates are timestamp-like.

conflicts.description: Foreign-key types differ from the string types of their referenced source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized target foreign keys to string to match their target primary keys.

conflicts.description: Runtime is recorded in minutes rather than a standard SI unit.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized runtime to seconds in runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is recorded in days.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized rental duration to seconds in rental_duration_seconds.

conflicts.description: The word rating is a homonym: IMDb stores an aggregate user score while Sakila stores an audience classification code.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the concepts separate as average_user_rating and content_rating_code.

conflicts.description: IMDb provides a language code on an alternative title while Sakila uses a surrogate language key and English language name.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved IMDb's value as language_code on alternative_title and retained Sakila's normalized language entity, avoiding an unsupported equivalence.

conflicts.description: Monetary amounts have no explicit source currency.
conflicts.resolution: Retained numeric amounts without asserting a currency.

conflicts.description: A geometry value contains multiple spatial coordinates in a non-generic source type.
conflicts.resolution: Represented it atomically as numeric latitude_degrees and longitude_degrees.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns encode arrays inside scalar strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized repeating values into profession, known-title, category, alternative-title type/attribute, title-credit, character, and special-feature child or bridge resources.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates searchable film text in a separate film_text table.
conflicts.resolution: Merged semantically identical title and description attributes into media_title with combined provenance.

conflicts.description: Episode hierarchy is stored in a relationship table rather than directly on title rows.
conflicts.resolution: Retained a normalized episode relationship resource with two distinct foreign keys to media_title.

conflicts.description: The address geometry is composite and not supported by the permitted generic target types.
conflicts.resolution: Decomposed it into atomic latitude and longitude fields.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to three title genres while Sakila models film-category as an explicit many-to-many relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized both as the title_category bridge.

conflicts.description: Title-person participation is represented by embedded lists, detailed principal rows, and a many-to-many actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized participation as title_credit rows, with normalized character rows and role indicators.

conflicts.description: Known-for titles are a multi-valued person-to-title association embedded in one column.
conflicts.resolution: Materialized person_known_title as a many-to-many bridge.

conflicts.description: A title can have multiple localized alternative-title rows distinguished only by per-title ordering.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled alternative_title as a one-to-many child entity with its own synthetic row identifier.

conflicts.description: A film can have many physical inventory copies and each copy belongs to one store.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved inventory_item as a distinct child entity between media titles and rentals.

conflicts.description: Equivalent media entities use natural alphanumeric and surrogate numeric key domains that can collide when represented as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Defined a canonical source-qualified media_title_id while preserving all corresponding source key provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person entities use unrelated identifier domains.
conflicts.resolution: Defined a canonical source-qualified person_id with both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: Ordering values are only unique within a parent title and are not declared source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced synthetic identifiers for alternative-title and title-credit rows while retaining ordering as a source attribute.

conflicts.description: Episode and rating tables omit declared primary keys even though each row is functionally identified by its title.
conflicts.resolution: Used episode_title_id and media_title_id respectively as target primary keys.

conflicts.description: Payment has a documented unique surrogate identifier but no declared source primary key.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted payment_id to the target primary key.

conflicts.description: Source bridge tables omit composite primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Applied composite keys to deterministic bridges and a synthetic key where heterogeneous credit structures require one normalized row identity.
